I’ve always been someone who likes precision—how things fit, how they function. As a mechanical engineer, it’s part of the job. But over the past year or so, that need for control has… shifted. My wife says I’m too thin, that I look frail. I’ve lost about 35 pounds since last winter, and I’m still losing. I weigh myself four or five times a day. If the number goes up even half a pound, I skip dinner. Water retention, salt, timing—it all matters. I measure my wrists, my waist, check the mirror from every angle.

She’s worried. Says I look sick. But I can’t risk gaining weight. That would mean losing control. And if I lose control… I don’t know what happens then. The scale doesn’t lie. It tells me exactly where I stand.

    D. Specific Phobia
